questions.title:
By the sea, or by the market?
Where will you live?
questions.talk:
An everyday view,
or everyday convenience!

options.title: Wake up to the sea!
options.cost: But groceries are a 30-minute drive away
options.reaction:
Let’s call the grocery run
a scenic drive!

options.title: Grocery runs in slippers!
options.cost: But the sea is a 30-minute drive away
options.reaction:
Visit the sea for fun,
shop with ease!

questions.title:
Weekend morning coffee:
which home will you have it in?
questions.talk:
Even a dreamy yard
comes with chores!

options.title: Stone walls and my own yard
options.detail: My own outdoor café in the sun
options.cost: But 2 hours of house and yard work every weekend
options.reaction:
Coffee in the yard!
Weeds, wait your turn.

options.title: An easy-care apartment
options.detail: Save the time you’d spend on upkeep
options.cost: But no yard of your own
options.reaction:
Weekends are precious,
so grab a coffee and go for a walk!

questions.title:
On the way to work:
the view or the distance?
questions.talk:
Working with a sea view —
did you think about the commute?

options.title: A workplace with a sea view
options.detail: Look up and there’s the sea
options.reaction:
With a view like this,
maybe the commute is worth it?

options.title: A 5-minute walk from home
options.detail: Time to spare before and after work
options.cost: But no sea view from work
options.reaction:
Let’s fill my day
with the commute time I saved!

questions.title:
If you worked in Jeju,
what kind of day would you choose?
questions.talk:
Between the work you love
and the days you want to rest!

options.title: Owning my dream little shop
options.detail: Running a space that reflects my taste
options.cost: But working weekends while others rest
options.reaction:
A space full of my taste!
Weekend guests, welcome in.

options.title: My usual work, from home
options.detail: Settling in while keeping my current work
options.cost: Put the shop dream on hold and rest on weekends

questions.title:
Dinner together tonight?
How close will you be with your neighbors?
questions.talk:
Friendly neighbors are nice,
and so is dinner on your own!

options.title: Eating often with neighbors
options.detail: Shared stories and a warm table
options.cost: But fewer evenings on your own
options.reaction:
One more side dish tonight!
It tastes better together.

options.title: A slow dinner on my own
options.detail: My time, on no one else’s schedule
options.cost: Make separate time to meet new friends
options.reaction:
Today’s menu and pace,
all up to me!

questions.title:
A text from a friend on the mainland:
“Can I come visit you in Jeju?”
questions.talk:
Friends are always welcome,
but think about your weekends too!

options.title: Invite them over monthly!
options.detail: Making Jeju memories with friends you miss
options.cost: But one weekend a month goes to hosting
options.reaction:
Time to start a booking
calendar for my place?

options.title: Mainland, every two months!
options.detail: Usual weekends are for my own life
options.cost: But I’m the one who flies to meet them
options.reaction:
My own time in Jeju,
double the joy when we meet!

questions.title:
Walking again next weekend?
Which path calls to you?
questions.talk:
Some things you notice because they’re familiar,
some because they’re new!

options.title: One path, all four seasons
options.detail: Noticing when flowers bloom and the wind shifts
options.cost: But your weekend walk is always the same path
options.reaction:
Same path,
but a different Jeju from yesterday!

options.title: A new path every week
options.detail: Adding a new memory to the map each time
options.cost: But you have to look up routes and transport every time
options.reaction:
Where to this week?
Even opening the map is exciting!

questions.title:
Even in Jeju, a day has 24 hours.
What will you put first?
questions.talk:
A slightly tough last question!
Where’s your heart right now?

options.title: Earn less, leave work early
options.detail: Enjoy a seaside walk after work every day
options.cost: But a tight budget for hobbies and eating out
options.reaction:
Let’s not miss today’s sunset.
My time matters too!

options.title: Work more, keep spare cash
options.detail: Plenty for hobbies and eating out
options.cost: But save your sea walks for the weekend
options.reaction:
Keep everyday life well stocked,
and look forward to the weekend sea!

variants: Starting the day in the yard
Coffee in hand, out to the yard. Sun first — the weeds can wait a bit.
Tidying up is done in no time. The effort saved today stays as time for me.
Opening a shop of my taste
I open the doors of my little shop and arrange the things I love. Who’ll drop by today?
At the laptop, my usual work, step by step. When it’s done, I head out to meet today’s Jeju.
“Want to have dinner together?” A meal shared with neighbors becomes the longest story of the day.
The menu, the music, how fast I eat — all up to me. I savor a long, quiet evening.
New seasons on the same path
Walking the path again, I spot small changes. A flower that wasn’t there last time is today’s news.
One more memory on the map
First, I pull up the map and transport options. Knowing there are paths I haven’t walked yet is today’s thrill.

0: The milk in the fridge may run out, but the sea outside the window stays!
Heading out for the sunset? Grab the car keys, not just your slippers.
2: The view fills your heart; the commute takes your time.
You can’t see the sea after work, but you can clearly see the time you saved.
7: Catch the sunset every day, and pick where to eat out a bit more carefully.
A comfortable budget for daily life, and an even more welcome weekend sea.

comments: You want to open a shop and leave work early too. Plan your opening hours carefully!
Tending the yard and finding new paths! Your weekend calendar might get quietly busy.
Dinners with neighbors and hosting friends from the mainland. Better find a free weekend first!
The sea every day and a short commute! You’ll be checking the distance between home and work closely.
You save time on groceries and after work, and spend it on yourself!
Once the meeting ends, your own time begins. From focus mode to rest mode, again today!

life.claim: You can climb to Baengnokdam, the summit of Hallasan, anytime without a reservation.
life.reveal:
The Seongpanak and Gwaneumsa trails to the summit need a reservation in advance (free).
Most other trails that don’t go to the summit need no reservation.
life.src: Hallasan National Park trail reservation guide · Related news reports

life.claim: In Jeju, there’s a custom of moving house during the week when ‘the gods go up to the sky and leave their posts.’
life.reveal:
It’s called ‘Singugan.’
From about 5 days after Daehan (Major Cold) to 3 days before Ipchun (Start of Spring), while the gods of the world went up to the sky to report to the Jade Emperor, people moved house and fixed up their homes.

life.claim: Jeju has so many tangerines that some places let you pay monthly rent in tangerines.
life.reveal:
No one pays rent in tangerines.
But there is ‘yeonse,’ where you pay a whole year’s rent at once.
That part’s real!
life.src: A fake card made up for fun

life.claim: Instead of a gate, old Jeju homes showed whether anyone was home by the number of wooden poles laid across the entrance.
life.reveal:
It’s called ‘jeongnang.’
Instead of a gate with doors, people laid wooden poles across the entrance, and the number of poles told whether anyone was home or not.
life.src: Local news reports on Jeju’s jeongnang

life.claim: Picking up turban shells or abalone from a Jeju village’s sea can count as theft.
life.reveal:
A village’s sea (its village fishing ground) is managed by the local fishing cooperative and tended by haenyeo (women divers).
Taking seafood from there can be punished as theft.
life.src: Korea Coast Guard guidance (Fishery Resources Management Act) · Related news reports

life.claim: If you move to Jeju, you have to pass a ‘Jeju language test’ within a year.
life.reveal:
There’s no test!
But UNESCO classifies the Jeju language as ‘critically endangered,’ so efforts to protect it continue.
life.src: A fake card made up for fun · UNESCO endangered languages classification (2010)

life.claim: In Jeju, people call neighborhood elders ‘samchun’ even if they’re not relatives.
life.reveal:
It’s a friendly way to address elders in the neighborhood, without much regard for gender or family ties.
The shop owner, the elder next door: all samchun!
life.src: Jeju National University, ‘A Study of Kinship Terms in the Jeju Dialect’

life.claim: These days, more people leave Jeju than move in.
life.reveal:
That’s been true three years in a row since 2023.
In 2025, 4,273 more people left than arrived.
Still, there are people who stay and make a life here.
life.src: Statistics Korea, Domestic Migration Statistics · ‘2025 Annual Jeju Regional Economic Trends’

peopleCards.claim: Someone in Jeju bought a ₩10,000 item online, and ₩5,000–6,000 in shipping was added on top.
peopleCards.reveal:
That’s more than half the price of the item.
One settler says it still makes them laugh in disbelief every time.
peopleCards.quote: an extra 5,000 to 6,000 won for shipping

peopleCards.claim: Jeju has so many tangerines that some places let you pay monthly rent in tangerines.
peopleCards.reveal:
No one pays rent in tangerines.
But there is a way of paying a whole year’s rent at once.
Check the next card!
peopleCards.src: A fake card made up for fun

peopleCards.claim: Jeju has ‘yeonse’: paying a whole year’s rent at once.
peopleCards.reveal: Since it takes a big lump sum all at once, one settler at first got by moving between one-month-stay rentals, suitcase in tow.
peopleCards.quote: paying a full year's rent in one lump sum

peopleCards.claim: There’s a settler whose revenue in Jeju grew more than tenfold compared with their salary at a Seoul job.
peopleCards.reveal:
It’s the story of a marketing CEO.
Of course, it’s one person’s experience, the result of the experience and client relationships they built up.
Before that came three years of trial and error.
peopleCards.quote: their revenue has now grown more than tenfold

peopleCards.claim: If you move to Jeju, you have to pass a ‘Jeju language test’ within your first year.
peopleCards.reveal:
There’s no test!
But UNESCO classifies the Jeju language as ‘critically endangered,’ so efforts to protect it continue.
peopleCards.src: A fake card made up for fun · UNESCO endangered languages classification (2010)

peopleCards.claim: These days, more people leave Jeju than move in.
peopleCards.reveal:
That’s been true three years in a row since 2023.
In 2025, 4,273 more people left than arrived.
Still, some people stayed.
peopleCards.src: Statistics Korea, Domestic Migration Statistics · ‘2025 Annual Jeju Regional Economic Trends’
peopleCards.quote: 4,273 more people moved out than moved in

peopleCards.claim: A settler in their third year in Jeju said this: “Coming just because you like nature might be a little risky.”
peopleCards.reveal:
Surprising, coming from someone who lives in Jeju, right?
But if you come because there’s something you really want to do, they say the possibilities are endless.
peopleCards.quote: coming simply because you like nature

peopleCards.claim: Someone came down to Jeju with just ₩500,000 in the bank and opened a photo studio and a goods shop.
peopleCards.reveal:
It’s true.
At first, they didn’t even plan to settle down.
The story in between? Coming up in your results!
peopleCards.quote: the money in hand was 500,000 won
